This isn't so easily described, I feel like I've done some pretty bad things, but the onus is mostly upon myself. Mostly in the form of guilt and self-conciousness.

But anyway, here's why I came here.

It was middle school, eigth grade. Usually I was the one getting punched around for laughs, and it didn't feel good. I was very socially awkward, obese, white, uncoordinated, you get the idea. Around this time, it had mostly died down, I had friends that cared, but I was still surpressed by a few different things. I understood that being bullied didn't feel good for me, but I had yet to comprehend what I could do to others. One day I tried it.

It was during class, downtime in the last 15 minutes or so. I decided to take probably the worst wise crack in my life. There was this beautiful girl sitting next to me, incredibly intelligent, well spoken, and just gorgeous. I of course had a bit of a crush, but that was all really. Her little sister had come in that day, nearly identical. Everybody was surprised, nobody had expected it. And of course, I was the dirty dan that had to say "But not everything is similar!" (she was about 13-14, her sister was still in elementary, so it's not too hard to imagine what stupid 14 year old me was thinking about) That is probably one of the stupidest things I've said, and I tried to snake out of it like a little prick.

I don't know what had come over me that day, I felt like a wreck and I didn't feel like me afterward. I used to be so careful, so bashful, and things like that just kept piling up. I never said anything that brasen or rude again, but I fell into traps like crazy from there on. I've been constantly misunderstood, awkward, clumsy, and indecisive for the past few years. The worst thing is, my arrogance only got worse, but I've finally understood that I have been arrogant.

When I was in elementary, the school counselors were always watching me, they thought I might have been mildly autistic. As I've grown older, that doesn't seem too far from the truth. It's yet to be determined, but I've always been five steps behind my peers when it comes to social situations. I don't want to make it an excuse though, and I find my behavior to be inexcusable and debilitating. I feel guilt for the stupidest things, I continually express similar pernicious behaviors, and I think it's just because I haven't been able to let go.

People used to perceive me as sensitive when I was very young, but I feel that was only because I was shy, and I always took a step back to learn. I think I need to fit into that pattern again. Years of guilt, bullying, and overthinking have densensitized me from who I was as a kid, and I just want to feel good about myself, I want to be good to others.

I know in a singular context my story may sound stupid, but it's been a landmark that's defined much of how I carried on as a young man. Not all of my life has been congested with being an asshole, and I have friends, but it's too much to deal with. This is where I stop.

My advice, if it's worth anything, is don't let your guilt pile up. Say your sorry as soon as it's appropriate, and if you do act like a dick, own up to it.
